questions.q: Canada has always been what kind of nation?
w: A nation that does not trade
A nation that only trades with Europe
A nation that grows only its own food
questions.e: Canada has always been a trading nation, and commerce continues to be the engine of economic growth.

questions.q: Which group of leading industrial countries is Canada a member of?
questions.e: Canada is one of the world's leading industrial nations. Discover Canada says the G8; since Russia was suspended in 2014 the group is called the G7.

questions.q: Canada has one of the ten largest economies in the world.
questions.e: Canada has one of the ten largest economies in the world.

questions.q: In 1988, Canada signed a free trade agreement with which country?
questions.e: In 1988, Canada signed a free trade agreement with the United States. Mexico became a partner in 1994 in the broader North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).

questions.q: Which agreement replaced NAFTA in 2020?
questions.e: NAFTA, which included Canada, the United States and Mexico from 1994, was replaced in 2020 by the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA). Discover Canada still mentions NAFTA.

questions.q: Which country is Canada's largest trading partner?
questions.e: Canada enjoys close relations with the United States, and each is the other's largest trading partner. Over three-quarters of Canadian exports go to the U.S.

questions.q: About what share of Canada's exports go to the United States?
questions.e: Over three-quarters of Canadian exports are destined for the United States.

questions.q: Canada and the United States share the longest undefended international border in the world.
questions.e: Canada and the United States have the longest undefended international border in the world.

questions.q: Canada is the largest foreign supplier of energy to the United States.
questions.e: Canada is the largest foreign supplier of energy, including oil, gas, uranium and electricity, to the United States.

questions.q: What are the three main types of industries in Canada?
questions.e: Canada has three main types of industries: service industries, manufacturing industries and natural resource industries.

questions.q: In which type of industry do most Canadians work?
questions.e: Service industries provide thousands of different jobs in areas like transportation, education, health care, construction, banking, communications, retail, tourism and government. More than 75% of working Canadians have jobs in service industries.

questions.q: About what percentage of working Canadians have jobs in service industries?
questions.e: More than 75% of working Canadians now have jobs in service industries.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a service industry job?
questions.e: Service industries include health care, education, transportation, construction, banking, communications, retail and tourism.

questions.q: Which of these products does Canada's manufacturing industry make?
questions.a: Cars, paper, aerospace equipment and food products
questions.e: Manufacturing industries make products to sell in Canada and around the world. These include paper, high technology equipment, aerospace technology, automobiles, machinery, food, clothing and many other goods.

questions.q: Which of these is a natural resource industry?
questions.e: Natural resource industries include forestry, fishing, agriculture, mining and energy.

questions.q: Natural resource industries have played an important part in Canada's history and development.
questions.e: Natural resource industries such as forestry, fishing, agriculture, mining and energy have played an important part in our history and development. Many communities still depend on them.

questions.q: A large part of Canada's exports comes from natural resources.
questions.e: A large percentage of Canada's exports are natural resource commodities.

questions.q: What is Canada's largest trading relationship based on?
questions.a: Trade in goods and services with the United States
questions.e: The United States is Canada's largest trading partner, with trade in energy, cars, machinery and many services.

questions.q: Canada's economy depends on trade with other countries.
questions.e: Canada has always been a trading nation. Trade creates jobs and helps Canadians enjoy one of the highest standards of living in the world.

questions.q: Canada has a market economy.
questions.e: Canada has a market economy in which most businesses are privately owned, with some services provided by governments.

questions.q: Which of these is part of the energy industry in Canada?
questions.e: Energy is a major natural resource industry in Canada, including oil and gas in Alberta and hydroelectricity in Quebec, Manitoba and British Columbia.

questions.q: Many Canadian cities have strong economies because of which kinds of jobs?
questions.a: Service jobs such as finance, health care and education
questions.e: Most Canadians live in cities and work in service industries such as finance, health care, education, retail and government.

questions.q: Most Canadians work in natural resource industries.
questions.e: More than 75% of working Canadians work in service industries.
